component_findings.compat_deprecation: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-4--c): Prior to Visual Studio 2015, MSVC did not guarantee binary compatibility across major versions; this was a deliberate, documented policy change toward long-term compatibility that has held for over a decade of releases (2015 through 2026).
component_findings.governance_change: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-4--c): Visual Studio maintains a stable C++ ABI across VS2015 (v140) through VS2026 (v145) despite C++ lacking a standard ABI
component_findings.release_cadence: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-4--c): The ISO C++ standard has followed a strict, documented three-year release cadence since C++11 (2011): C++11, C++14, C++17, C++20, C++23, with C++26 in progress and C++29 already the next planned standard.
component_findings.release_integrity: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-4--c): C++ has been on a three-year release schedule since 2012 with C++29 as the next planned standard
component_findings.support_policy: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-4--c): C++23, formally ISO/IEC 14882:2024, published in 2024 and replaced by C++26 in March 2026

metric.toolchain_stability_release_matur.limitations: C++ has no single unified toolchain vendor, so stability evidence is aggregated across GCC/Clang/MSVC and the ISO standard; ABI stability is a documented Microsoft-specific commitment rather than a universal cross-vendor ISO guarantee, which slightly discounts the compatibility-guarantees and stability-commitments sub-scores.
metric.toolchain_stability_release_matur.selection_rule: Score current observable release/support practices. Language age and first-release date are context only and never directly score.
